facts: Weronika Łajewska is affiliated with the University of Stavanger.
The research paper addresses information preservation in prompt compression for large language models.
The study proposes methods to improve the preservation of critical content during the compression process.
The research involves collaboration between academic institutions and industry, including Amazon and the Technical University of Catalonia.
The paper proposes a comprehensive evaluation framework for prompt compression techniques.
The authors achieved a +23% improvement in downstream performance with their enhanced soft prompting method.
The study reports an increase of 8 BERTScore points in grounding accuracy.
The enhanced method demonstrated 2.7× better entity preservation compared to previous techniques.
Recent advances in large language models have enabled their application to tasks requiring long contexts and in-context learning.
The paper proposes a holistic evaluation framework examining downstream performance, grounding of compressed context, and information preservation.
Modified xRAG achieves a 23% improvement on downstream tasks and 2.7× more preserved entities.
PISCO achieves the best compression-effectiveness tradeoff in long-context scenarios.
Prompt compression improves LLM efficiency by creating reduced-size approximate representations of prompts.
Hard prompting methods may disrupt grammar and require re-encoding.
Soft prompting methods achieve higher compression rates but lack explainability.
Current evaluation of compression methods relies primarily on downstream tasks across datasets like HotpotQA and QuAC.
The evaluation framework for prompt compression methods includes benchmarking data design for long-form QA and document summarization.
The compression quality evaluation framework measures downstream task performance using metrics like BERTScore and Exact Match.
Grounding is assessed via FABLES to measure how well key information from the original context is preserved.
Performance comparisons of various compression methods against the Mistral-7B baseline show drops ranging from 1% to 64% depending on the task.

The analysis evaluates three prompt compression methods: xRAG, PISCO, and LLMLingua. All compression methods cause 3-55% relative performance losses. xRAG shows a 30-50 point drop in grounding scores compared to uncompressed baselines. PISCO maintains superior information retention through its 8-embedding encoding capacity.
xRAG w/ Sentence PT + FT increases entity preservation from 13% to 20%.
xRAG w/ Two-Step PT + FT achieves a 23% relative improvement on HotpotQA.
xRAG variants maintain competitive compression rates of 4x-12x.
PISCO remains state-of-the-art for long-context compression.
Current compression techniques fail to preserve detailed information at high compression rates.
The proposed solution includes multi-token context understanding through sequence-level distillation.
Context-aware adaptive compression dynamically adjusts compression rates based on input complexity.
Hybrid soft-hard prompting combines soft prompts for general context with hard prompts to retain critical details.
The paper evaluates prompt compression methods in long-context generation tasks.
The study identifies that existing compression techniques often fail to preserve detailed information.
The authors propose improvements to the xRAG soft compression method.
The proposed improvements achieve a performance gain of up to 23% on downstream tasks.
The study focuses exclusively on Mistral-7B.
The evaluation is restricted to English benchmarks.
Only one representative baseline per compression technique category was examined.
The section includes 11 academic references from major NLP venues.
Mistral-7B Instruct v0.2 was trained on two 8-GPU A100 instances over approximately 16 hours.
The dataset used for training contained 1,128,075 samples, with 628,003 having valid context after filtering.
The study evaluates compression methods including xRAG variants, LLMLingua, and PISCO across multiple datasets.
The Mistral-7B baseline achieves grounding scores ranging from 0.42 to 0.84 across datasets.
